title: Seeking lessons from Tio and Walter DeVoyne; first job
summary: Lorenzo Tio is leaving for New York, so he studies with Walter DeVoyne and then plays his first house-party job with a piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Did anybody have a banging system at all in those days that you knew?

Not that I know of, you know. Mm-hmm. And, um, well I took it and tried to practice on it. I didn't know what I was doing. So I tried to get Lorenzo Teo to teach me. I went to Lorenzo's house. He was staying on Seminar Street. I went to Lorenzo's house. And he agreed to teach me. He told me, he said, he told me to go buy a book. I told Angie and come to his house the following Wednesday.
Is that the young Lorenzo Teo? Yes.

Not the real old man? No, not the old man. So I went to his house that Wednesday with my book and here he comes to the door and I told him, well I care for my lesson. He said, well I'm sorry I can't give you any lessons. He said, because I'm leaving. I'm going to New York. Oh, that's bad.
It didn't happen. That was P-Roll. That's about it. So I left there.

Well, who could I try again? Well all the musicians was working. Pico and all those folks, they were working so much they didn't care to be bothered with teaching anybody. So I asked Pico, well he didn't have time to get on all this. The best thing I could do, well there was a fella that some fellas told me about, a fella by the name of Walter DeVoyne. He would play a little clarinet, you know. Well he was a tinsmith, so he was always willing to help somebody, you know. So I had a couple of fellas going to him. Well I went to him and he started me off.
Did you start with that same method then?

Yeah, with that same method. And he started me off. Well after I went to him for a while, for I'd say two, three months after I was gone to him. Well he learned me all he could. So I quit. Then by that time I lost practice, you know, my home trying to play numbers and I learned how to play a few numbers and I got to, I played a little job. A fella came and asked me to come play a job with him, just piano and clarinet. It was on a hollow night, I've forgotten what night it was. Just sort of party? Yeah, it was a house party. So a little galo it was.

So I went, I was wondering all the while, you know, I was going to make out. I had never practiced with a piano, with a nut. So I went there and we played the part where we made out alright. That was the first job I played.
